labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p1_alpha_cone_appui
labels.notes: prop1_coneAppui (l.267) is a correct, non-vacuous theorem: W convex, a, b in W, a TFAE of (1)-(4) when b != a, -a and of (1),(3),(4) when b = a or -a. Item (2) is DemiDroitesRencontrent (l.124): every half-line IsDemiDroiteJoignant a h contained in supportK {a, b} meets W, with h the library's OPEN half-line halfLine A w (ends a, a' excluded). That is a reading of the printed (2), and the row's truth depends on it. OQ-162 (a) (OPEN) records the CLOSED reading of the same noun « demi-droites » joining a to a' in Déf. 1′, two paragraphs earlier (l.889-892), which the proof of Prop. 1 invokes for (2) <=> (3). Under that closed reading (2) holds for every b, because each closed half-line contains a in W, and (1) <=> (2) fails (prop1_instance_end: the arc of S(1), a, b its ends). Under the open reading Prop. 1 holds and Déf. 1′ fails (coneAppui_ne_demiDroitesW: the union misses a'). So no single convention makes both Déf. 1′ and Prop. 1 true as printed. One of them needs a correction, and which one depends on how OQ-162 (a) is ruled. The planner's evidence says Prop. 1 'does not wait on OQ-162 (a)'. That holds for the step through Déf. 1′ when b != a, a′, but not for (2)'s own wording. CAMPAIGN.md: 'partial — … or a reading'. The REPORT itself classes the hypothesis as 'here: reading' and still sets status closed and marked: true, with findings: [].

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p2_dual_cone_appui_sature
labels.notes: prop2_coneAppui (l.329): any bilinear form B (hypothesis (a) of § 3 only, nothing from (b)-(d)), IsConvexPart W (the [sic] reading of « W ⊂ K(S(E)) »), a in W. Both conclusions are carried: D(W_a) ⊆ D(W), and for m1 in D(W_a), m2 in D(W) with AlphaK (D B W) m1 m2, m2 in D(W_a). No extra hypothesis. prop2_instance shows the inclusion is strict on the arc.

labels.label: bzdef:c3s4d3_orthogonalite_points
labels.notes: OrthPts (l.371) is the dot product of the chosen representatives. Each sentence of Déf. 3 is a lemma: independence of the representatives (orthPts_iff, any IsRep M m, IsRep P p), symmetry (orthPts_comm), and the reformulation through D({p}) containing m and m′ (orthPts_iff_D). def3_instance is non-trivial: a0 is orthogonal to b1, and a0 is not orthogonal to itself.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p3_dual_cone_appui
labels.notes: prop3_coneAppui (l.403): for any a in S(n), W convex with a ∈ W, D(W_a) = {m in D(W) | OrthPts m a}. The a ∈ W is honest as a domain condition: Déf. 1 (l.881) defines W_a only under « W ∈ K(S(E)), a ∈ W », so the printed W_a presupposes it. It is not an added hypothesis on a defined object. The identity also fails outside that domain for nonempty W, not only at W = ∅ (D_coneAppui_empty_ne): take W = {b} with b != ±a, where D(W_a) = {⟨·,b⟩ ≥ 0, ⟨·,a⟩ ≤ 0}. That supports the domain reading. prop3_instance (D(W_a) = {b1} on the arc) is real and goes through prop3_coneAppui.

findings.what: Prop. 1 is marked as fully certified, but its truth rests on reading « demi-droites » as open half-lines in (2). OQ-162 (a), still OPEN, records the closed reading of the same word in Déf. 1′ of the same section, and Prop. 1's proof invokes that definition. Under the closed reading (2) is always true and Prop. 1 is false as printed (prop1_instance_end). Under the open reading Prop. 1 holds and Déf. 1′ is false as printed (coneAppui_ne_demiDroitesW). The section is not consistent under either single convention, so the mark settles a question the author has not ruled. CAMPAIGN.md makes a row taken under a reading `partial`.
